title: Teams with agents that contain duplicated produced_message_types result in an ValueError exception
body:
### What happened?

**Describe the bug**
On 0.53.0 output_content_type for agents is automatically registered into the team [Code Reference](https://github.com/abhinav-aegis/autogen/blob/2d3f83b809516906e7329518a28c794dffcf42e3/python/packages/autogen-agentchat/src/autogen_agentchat/teams/_group_chat/_base_group_chat.py#L72-L79).  When a team is comprised of agents that share the same output_content_type then a ValueError is raised.

**To Reproduce**
Add into a team 2 agents with the same Pydantic model as output_content_type.

```
ValueError: Message type <class 'autogen_agentchat.messages.StructuredMessage[<TestModel>]'> is already registered.
```

**Expected behavior**
Only register structured messages that have not been registered previously.

**Screenshots**
If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem.

**Additional context**
I have added https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/pull/6354 for your consideration


### Which packages was the bug in?

Python AgentChat (autogen-agentchat>=0.4.0)

### AutoGen library version.

Python 0.5.3

### Other library version.

_No response_

### Model used

gpt-4o

### Model provider

OpenAI

### Other model provider

_No response_

### Python version

3.11

### .NET version

None

### Operating system

MacOS

linked_prs.title: Avoid re-registering a message type already registered
linked_prs.body:

## Why are these changes needed?

This change avoid re-registering a structured message already registered to the team by a previous agent also included in the team.

This issue occurs when agents share Pydantic models as output format

## Related issue number

Closes #6353

## Checks

- [ ] I've added tests (if relevant) corresponding to the changes introduced in this PR.
- [ ] I've made sure all auto checks have passed.

ai_judgment.response: Yes. This is an agent issue because it involves a bug in the agent system related to memory initialization and content errors, specifically the improper handling of `output_content_type` registration for agents within a team, which is unique to agent systems.
